title: One rule: add two
alt: Starting from three, adding two gives five, seven, then nine. All four counts are odd.

title: Rate, change, and starting amount
alt: A tank starts with five liters. Two liters per minute for three minutes adds six liters, leaving eleven liters.

title: Same fence, different area
alt: A three-by-five rectangle encloses fifteen square meters. A four-by-four square encloses sixteen. Both use sixteen meters of fence.

title: The same books, counted each day
alt: Monday has eight books, Tuesday eleven, Wednesday nine, Thursday fourteen. The changes are plus three, minus two, and plus five.

title: A one-way rule
alt: All club members have badges. Jo is shown inside the members group, itself inside badge holders. A possible guest also has a badge, outside the members group.

title: Use the second input
alt: The inputs are red first and blue second. The rule returns blue. Changing the selected input position changes the result.

title: Use the first input
alt: The inputs are red first and blue second. The rule returns red. Changing the selected input position changes the result.

title: Sell one ticket
alt: Four tickets become three when one is sold. A nonnegative count after selling requires at least one ticket beforehand.

title: The same books, selected by a rule
alt: Books B1 and B4 match gardening AND available. B2 is available but astronomy; B3 is gardening but unavailable.

title: Both wait; neither lets go
alt: Jo holds the printer and waits for Sam's scissors. Sam holds the scissors and waits for Jo's printer. Their waiting forms a loop.

title: One action, two kinds of fact
alt: Opening the cupboard changes its door from closed to open. The cup remains inside in both states.

title: One action, two kinds of fact
alt: Opening the cupboard changes its door from closed to open. The poster remains inside in both states.

title: Pick one bead
alt: Two red and three blue beads are equally likely to be picked, giving two red chances out of five.

title: Pick one token
alt: One green and three yellow tokens are equally likely to be picked. The image supplies the starting contents only.

title: Observe a clue; or change a setting
alt: In the observation model, heat affects both sprinklers and drink buying. Under an intervention setting sprinklers, heat still affects drink buying, but no longer determines the sprinkler setting.

title: Count orders; then count what they need
alt: Two selected orders each need one crate. They require two crates altogether. Starting with three crates leaves one.

title: A new obstacle changes the choices
alt: Without an obstacle, the straight path connects two points. With a cabinet blocking that route, an allowed path goes around it. The goal can remain shortest length.

title: An average is not a path
alt: Two fair independent coin tosses make four equally likely paths. Their final positions are plus two, zero, zero, and minus two.

title: A description is not its execution
alt: One panel shows a stored recipe card. The other shows using that recipe to bake. Keeping a description does not automatically run its instructions.

title: Arrangement changes the rule
alt: In the lesson's parentheses notation, two empty marks beside one another simplify to one mark. A mark inside a mark simplifies to the unmarked form, shown as blank space rather than zero.

title: Check each pair
alt: The observer cannot distinguish 20 from 21 degrees or 21 from 22, so those pairs have edges. There is no edge between 20 and 22 degrees.

title: Same record, different originals
alt: The pairs zero and two, and one and one, both average to one. Repeating that average rebuilds one and one; the record alone cannot identify which original pair was used.

title: Check the kind of input
alt: An instruction from date to text can connect to one from text to printed card. A photograph does not fit an input that specifically requires text.

title: If sealed, then labeled
alt: Both a sealed labeled jar and an open labeled jar obey the one-way rule. Seeing a label alone therefore does not establish that a jar is sealed.

title: Different questions, different tools
alt: Ten unranked tiles name rates, space, steps, proof, programs, data, interaction, chance, operators, and observation. They are entry points, not a ladder.

title: Make the idea travel
alt: Read an example, make a prediction, explain your reasoning, and change one thing. Repeat with the changed problem.

title: Start, rate, time
alt: The practice problem starts with twelve chairs and adds four chairs per minute for three minutes. The final count is left for the reader.

title: Change one dimension
alt: A rectangular photograph is three units wide and five units tall. The reader can increase either dimension by one.

title: A sequence of headcounts
alt: Four room headcounts are ten, fourteen, thirteen, and eighteen, in that order.

title: Four sides; different shapes
alt: A square and a nonsquare rectangle both have four sides. The rectangle is a counterexample to reversing the rule that every square has four sides.

title: Work backward from the promise
alt: An unknown starting score is reduced by three points. The required result is nonnegative. The starting condition is left for the reader.

title: Two conditions, four songs
alt: Song A is short but not a favorite. B is a favorite but not short. C is both. D is neither. No answer selection is marked.

title: New tools, the same waiting pattern
alt: One cook holds the bowl and waits for the whisk. The other holds the whisk and waits for the bowl.

title: Pass a name; gain a connection
alt: Before the message, Alice knows a and b, and Bob knows a. Alice sends b on a. Afterward Bob knows both a and b; Alice keeps both names.

title: Same arrow, different coordinates
alt: The same northeast arrow has components three east and two north, or two north and minus three west. Only the coordinate directions change.

title: One stretch, two descriptions
alt: The same linear map doubles east-west lengths and leaves north-south lengths unchanged. In east-north coordinates the diagonal factors are two and one; in north-west coordinates they are one and two.

title: Shared edges cancel
alt: Two adjacent unit squares are traced counterclockwise. The shared edge is traversed up and down. These opposite traversals cancel, leaving six outside unit edges.

title: Which edges form the boundary?
alt: Eight square tiles fill a three-by-three grid except for the missing center tile. No perimeter totals or walking directions are supplied.

title: Turn the arrow; keep the axes
alt: In fixed real and imaginary axes, multiplying three plus two i by i rotates the arrow counterclockwise by a quarter turn to minus two plus three i.

title: Go around a point without touching it
alt: A counterclockwise circular contour surrounds zero. The example function one divided by z is undefined at zero, but the circle itself avoids zero.

title: A small weighted-history model
alt: Record A has changes four, zero, zero; record B has zero, four, zero. Weighting those intervals by one-quarter, one-half, and one gives scores one and two. These teaching weights do not define a fractional derivative.

title: What does the action do twice?
alt: The swap operator A sends the pair two, five to five, two. A second application returns two, five. Two swaps act as the identity on every pair.

title: Two different meanings of “square”
alt: Matrix multiplication squares the swap matrix to give the identity matrix. Squaring each entry separately leaves the swap matrix unchanged.

title: One token, two possible choices
alt: A single token can be exchanged for one snack or for one drink. The two branches show alternatives; each purchase consumes the token.

title: Allocate a resource to each task
alt: One of two separate tokens is exchanged for a snack and the other for a drink. Each token supports just one of the two purchases.

title: One card, two views
alt: The chosen card A is a red circle. Jo sees only color, leaving A or B possible. Sam sees only shape, leaving A or C possible.

title: Everyone hears: “The card is red”
alt: After a truthful public announcement of red, Jo still allows A and B. Sam rules out blue card C, leaving only A.

title: Which crates share a record?
alt: Batch A contains ready crates 1 and 2. Batch B contains ready crate 3 and not-ready crate 4. Batch C contains not-ready crates 5 and 6. The scanner reports only the batch letter.

title: Definite, possible, and unresolved
alt: The upper approximation contains crates 1, 2, 3, and 4. Inside it, the lower approximation contains 1 and 2 and the unresolved boundary contains 3 and 4. Crates 5 and 6 are outside the upper approximation.

title: A measurement guides a later action
alt: Qubit 1 carries the input and qubit 2 is prepared. After linking them, qubit 1 is measured. Its ordinary outcome bit controls a correction on qubit 2, which is the output. The dashed path carries the recorded bit.

title: Use the recorded bit
alt: With bit zero the target state is left alone. With bit one the output is X of the target and a further X returns the target. This uses X squared equals the identity.

title: Same sequences, different choices
alt: Machine A accepts payment then offers both tea and coffee. Machine B has two payment transitions, one to tea-only and one to coffee-only. Both allow pay-tea and pay-coffee traces, but B can commit to one drink during payment.

title: Set watering; keep its effects
alt: The observational graph has weather affecting watering and growth, and watering affecting growth. Setting watering removes the incoming weather-to-watering arrow while retaining the other arrows. The crossed dashed line marks the removed arrow.

title: Compare the same weather mix
alt: The observed watered and unwatered groups have success rates 50 and 70 percent and different weather mixes. Adjusting both to half mild and half hot gives intervention rates 65 and 55 percent under the stated model.

title: Build a rule that keeps the second
alt: K I receives tea and cake. Applying K to I and tea leaves I, which receives cake and returns cake.

title: S supplies the same input twice
alt: S K K tea rewrites to two copies of the expression K tea, with the left applied to the right. K keeps tea and discards the right expression, leaving tea.

title: One recipe, two chosen types
alt: The same twice recipe uses add three to send four to seven to ten, and uses flip to send on to off to on. Each row keeps one value type throughout.

title: Can the output go back in?
alt: A number-to-text label maker accepts four and returns the text four. That text cannot enter its number input for the second use.

title: Try the credit program
alt: A starting balance of five credits doubles to ten, then loses three to finish at seven. Four doubles to eight, then finishes at five and misses the goal of at least seven.

title: Work backward from the promise
alt: Reasoning backward begins with the goal of at least seven, moves to at least ten before deducting three, and then at least five before doubling. The program itself runs in the opposite order.

title: A fixed total and a falling count
alt: At successive loop checks, waiting and finished counts are three and zero, two and one, one and two, then zero and three. The sum remains three while waiting falls by one.

title: Separate cells: preserve the rest
alt: Before an update, p points to address twelve holding four, and q to address twenty-seven also holding four. After storing nine through p, only address twelve changes; address twenty-seven still holds four.

title: Different names, one shared cell
alt: Both p and q point to the same address twelve, initially holding four. Writing nine through p changes that one cell, so reading through q now also gives nine.

title: Grow the square by one step
alt: A three-by-three square has nine old tiles. Extending it to four by four adds a row of four and a column of three, for seven new tiles and sixteen total.

title: Take the differences again
alt: The values zero, one, four, nine, sixteen have first differences one, three, five, seven. Their second differences are two, two, two.

title: Three samples, three rate estimates
alt: Tank readings are six liters at minute one, nine at minute two, and fourteen at minute three. Backward and forward one-minute changes give rates three and five; the two-minute centered comparison gives four liters per minute.

title: Straight joins estimate a curved flow
alt: Two graphs show the known flow curve q equals time squared from zero to four minutes. Straight joins using two-minute steps give twenty-four liters; one-minute steps give twenty-two. Both lie above the curved flow, whose exact total is twenty-one and one-third liters.

title: The readings can miss a whole pulse
alt: Zero flow throughout and a triangular pulse share zero-valued readings at minutes zero and one. The pulse peaks at four liters per minute halfway through and adds two liters that the endpoint-only estimate misses.

title: Where does the amount stop changing?
alt: With inflow six liters per minute, amounts four, eight, twelve, and sixteen liters produce net rates plus four, plus two, zero, and minus two. Below twelve the amount rises; above twelve it falls.

title: Recalculate the rate halfway through
alt: One one-minute Euler step goes from four to eight liters. Two half-minute steps go from four to six to seven and a half liters. The continuous model gives about seven point one five liters at one minute.

title: Solve in a different form
alt: The time equation and starting value are transformed into an algebra equation. Solving gives the transformed answer; the inverse transform returns the amount as a function of time. The starting four liters is included in the first step.

title: Water plus gap always makes twelve
alt: Three bars each span the twelve-liter equilibrium amount. At the start, water four plus gap eight makes twelve. At one minute, about seven point one five plus four point eight five makes twelve. At two minutes, about nine point zero six plus two point nine four makes twelve.

title: Match the topic, then check availability
alt: Jo's gardening request matches available books B1 and B4. Jo's astronomy request matches B2. Sam's gardening request matches B1 and B4. Lee's history request has no match.

title: Both properties must hold in one row
alt: In a two-row catalog, B2 is astronomy and available, while B3 is gardening and unavailable. Each desired property appears somewhere, but no single row is both gardening and available.

title: Connect records through a shared value
alt: A request has reader Jo and topic Gardening. A book has ID B1, title Small Gardens, topic Gardening, and availability Yes. The same topic value fills the topic slot in both records; the output keeps Jo and B1.

title: Does every request have a match?
alt: Jo's Gardening and Astronomy requests are covered, Sam's Gardening request is covered, and Lee's History request is missing. Dee has no requests. The every-request condition passes Jo, Sam, and Dee; requiring at least one request removes Dee.

title: Two preparations, one shared handoff
alt: Starting with neither preparation done, folding makes only Jo ready and clearing makes only Sam ready. Either preparation can happen first. After both, the handoff can occur, followed by displaying the poster.

title: Agree on the next shared event
alt: In the blocked version Jo's first event is receipt and Sam's first event is handoff, so no shared first event is possible. In the repaired version both begin with handoff and then receipt, so they can agree at each step.

title: Move a boundary with its contents
alt: Before entry, bag and van are side by side, and parcel is inside bag. After bag enters van, parcel remains inside bag, and bag is inside van.

title: Leave the van, or remove the bag?
alt: Starting from parcel inside bag inside van, exiting moves the intact bag beside the van. Opening bag instead removes its boundary, leaving parcel directly inside van. The two outcomes preserve the parcel but change different boundaries.

title: Receiving is not yet reading
alt: The same ciphertext C is tested with two keys. Decryption with the matching key K recovers print one poster and continues. A different key J does not enable that decryption step.

title: Copying a message can repeat an action
alt: A printer that remembers no earlier requests accepts ciphertext C twice and prints two posters. A printer that checks a matching one-use challenge accepts the first valid response, marks the challenge used, and rejects a repeated response, printing one poster.
